name: Antique Brass
lede: Antique Brass pairs "antique," meaning aged in look, with brass, the copper-and-zinc metal, for a dulled metallic tan named in the Crayola crayon line.

sections.title: Aged metal, not aged color
sections.body: The name is a modifier plus a material: "antique" signals the dulled, oxidized look of old metal, attached to brass, an alloy of copper and zinc [1]. Wikipedia credits it to the Crayola crayon list, with no earlier dictionary record in the sources consulted here [1]. The ISCC-NBS system filed the same tone in 1955, block 109, a light grayish olive, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates it to 1913, plate 14 J 4 [2]. A Japanese library list carries the same hue as 白茶 (*shiracha*), "white tea-colored" [2]. Its nearest named look-alike is [[orange-cinnamon]], with [[raw-sienna]], [[light-cinnamon]] and [[beige-red]] close by in the same tan-brown family [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this tan-brown in 892 of 23,781 paintings (3.75 percent, as photographed), more common than 83 percent of named colors here [4]. It peaks in the 1500s, at 2.1 times the expected rate (109 of 2,231 paintings from that century), and plays an accent color in 62 percent of the paintings where it dominates [4]. It is most over-represented in Indian paintings (2.3 times expected) and shares canvases with Light Ochraceous-Salmon more than chance [4]. The earliest matching canvas dates to the year 900, centuries before the name was recorded; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first, and a look-alike hue, not the metal itself [4].
